question_frame: PLAN-01 v2 target-mechanism search: through 2024-12-31, identify peer-reviewed evidence linking LRRK2 to Parkinson disease, tracing initial PARK8/LRRK2 genetic discovery, pathogenic and risk variants, kinase/GTPase mechanisms, physiological substrates, and null, discordant, model-dependent, penetrance-limiting, or replication evidence that constrains causal strength or generality. Scope includes human genetics and neuropathology, biochemical studies, cells, iPSC-derived systems, and animal models; all languages are eligible when an interpretable abstract or accessible evidence supports screening. Primary studies drive conclusions, while reviews support terminology and linked-record expansion. Outcomes include variant association and segregation, penetrance, enzymatic activity, substrate phosphorylation, pathway effects, neuronal phenotypes, and relevance to familial and idiopathic Parkinson disease.

inclusion_criteria: Publication date or online-first date is on or before 2024-12-31.
Peer-reviewed primary studies directly examine LRRK2 genetics in Parkinson disease or LRRK2 enzymology, substrates, pathways, or phenotypes relevant to the disease relationship.
Human genetic evidence reports association, segregation, penetrance, ancestry, phenotype, or neuropathology for a specified LRRK2 variant or locus.
Mechanistic evidence specifies the LRRK2 perturbation, biological system, assay, comparator, and measured enzymatic, substrate, pathway, or disease-relevant outcome.

Biochemical substrate claims include direct phosphorylation evidence or orthogonal endogenous validation; physiological-substrate claims additionally require detection or perturbation in cells, tissues, organisms, or patient-derived material.
Null, negative, discordant, replication, correction, expression-of-concern, and retraction records are eligible when they test or qualify an included claim.
Reviews and meta-analyses are eligible for terminology expansion, anchor checking, and linked-reference discovery, with causal conclusions traced to primary studies.
Studies in humans, human-derived cells, nonhuman animals, cultured cells, or purified systems are eligible when the organism and model limitations are explicitly recorded.
All languages are eligible when the title, abstract, or accessible text provides enough information for reliable screening and extraction.
exclusion_criteria: Studies mentioning LRRK2 or Parkinson disease without data bearing on genetics, enzymatic mechanism, physiological substrates, downstream pathways, or limitations of those claims.
Non-peer-reviewed commentary, news, meeting abstracts without sufficient methods or results, and narrative opinion lacking traceable primary evidence.
Drug efficacy studies that do not report target engagement, LRRK2 pathway biomarkers, substrate phosphorylation, or mechanistic outcomes relevant to the brief.
Non-Parkinson disorders are excluded unless their experimental evidence directly identifies or challenges an LRRK2 enzyme mechanism or physiological substrate relevant to Parkinson disease.
Purely predicted substrates or interactions lacking experimental validation.
Duplicate publications are consolidated by PMID, DOI, cohort, and experiment; the most complete record is retained while linked reports and every query occurrence remain recorded.
Records whose methods, model, variant, or outcome cannot be determined sufficiently for claim-level appraisal.
stop_rules: Execute queries in the fixed order Q01 through Q12 and preserve each event, exact query, retrieval timestamp, result set, and query-to-record links.
Complete all planned PubMed waves unless the predefined limit of 12 query events is reached; budget exhaustion must be reported without silently adding queries.
The sentinel wave must recover the independent 2004 genetic-discovery anchors and at least one primary Rab-substrate anchor; missing anchors trigger alias review within the existing query budget.
Screen challenge evidence before synthesis and explicitly classify null, discordant, model-dependent, correction, and retraction findings.

For expansion, examine linked PubMed records and reference leads from included reviews or anchors; stop after two consecutive expansion passes add no decision-relevant genetic, enzyme, substrate, physiological, or limiting evidence.

Stop when all available-source queries are complete, anchors are recovered, duplicate resolution is stable, and further PubMed retrieval is unlikely to change the mechanistic conclusion or its uncertainty.

Escalate conflicting duplicate reports, incompatible variant annotations, contradictory substrate results, or uncertain publication dates for manual resolution and fail closed on unresolved identity conflicts.
Separate execution completion, evidence outcome, and confidence in the final mechanism; completion of the plan alone does not establish a causal mechanism.
coverage_gaps: Only PubMed is available; citation-graph and DOI-metadata services for systematic forward and backward citation expansion are unavailable.
Trial registries and regulator sources are unavailable, limiting independent assessment of clinical target-engagement, intervention status, and safety evidence.
Preprint sources are unavailable, so recent unreviewed findings through the as-of date may be missed.
Dedicated variant databases and primary genomic repositories are unavailable, limiting independent verification of variant classification, population frequency, and raw association data.
Patents and chemistry databases are unavailable; medicinal-chemistry prior art and compound-level selectivity evidence are outside retrieval coverage.
Full-text availability is not guaranteed by PubMed, which may constrain appraisal of methods, negative results, online-first dates, and supplementary phosphoproteomic data.
